title: Steve Jobs on Design, Objects and the Web: Wired's "The Next Insanely Great Thing" (1996)
summary: In a 1996 Wired interview, Jobs defines design as how something works, calls creativity connecting experiences, and argues the Web must stay simple to beat Microsoft. He also says technology cannot fix education or change the world, and describes choosing a washing machine as a design exercise.

principles.text: Design is how it works, not just how it looks.
principles.quote: Some people think design means how it looks. But of course, if you dig deeper, it's really how it works.

principles.text: Great design requires deep, passionate understanding, not a quick swallow.
principles.quote: To design something really well, you have to get it. You have to really grok what it's all about. It takes a passionate commitment to really thoroughly understand something, chew it up, not just quickly swallow it.

principles.text: Creativity is connecting experiences; creative people just see the connections.
principles.quote: Creativity is just connecting things. When you ask creative people how they did something, they feel a little guilty because they didn't really do it, they just saw something.

principles.text: Broader understanding of human experience produces better design.
principles.quote: The broader one's understanding of the human experience, the better design we will have.

principles.text: Design choices reflect values and trade-offs, worth debating deeply.
principles.quote: We ended up talking a lot about design, but also about the values of our family.

principles.text: Simplicity drives adoption; resist complexity that slows ubiquity.
principles.quote: One of the major reasons for the Web's proliferation so far is its simplicity. A lot of people want to make the Web more complicated.
